scope: 32 feature-gap targets; source states and evidence are deliberately separate. Historical common-profile passes are contextual, never automatic target qualification.

adapter-file.boundary: Linux C adapter over Legacy native file storage. Each feature has separate reference/artifact evidence; historical common-v1 logical behavior uses compatibility scans/buffers and native formats.

file-legacy.boundary: Public default; native duplicates, savepoints, borrowed snapshots, backup and manual maintenance exist. New backlog targets require their own evidence.

file-cohort.boundary: Shared native API, different publication metadata; Legacy evidence does not independently qualify its publication/lifecycle behavior.

file-indexed.boundary: Shared native API, indexed publication metadata; retain separate migration/publication/lifecycle gates.

resident.boundary: Experimental bounded anonymous page pool plus WAL; no duplicates/savepoints/checkpoint/export/replication or WAL retirement; records cap 4080 bytes, WAL 256 MiB.

hybrid.boundary: Experimental backend with existing checkpoint and retirement APIs; evaluate reuse without inheriting qualification.

range-v6.boundary: Experimental format6; range-lifecycle enables independent read-only capture/export. Retention/reclaim/compact/replication and adapter access remain unqualified or unsupported.

features.limits: Qualified for the exact Linux Legacy-backed C adapter artifact and pinned LMDB 1.0.2 API profile: dirty unpublished owners, clean/readonly/child consumption, metadata guards, cursor invalidation, final publication/abort and exact initial IDs. The combined 61-check feature replay, fourteen-stage Linux gate and 133 real C lifecycle I/O failures pass. Matched ordinary-operation change budgets and the predeclared controlled tail review pass; tmpfs initial-load regression 8.91% remains outside the accepted budget. Evidence: conformance/features/m3-f02-f03-qualified. Other native backends remain independently unqualified. Range preparation remains unsupported; this is not restart-recoverable distributed two-phase commit. G03/G04 and M1/G05 performance acceptance remain separate.

features.target: Roll back the eligible last commit

tests.case: 55 valid modern rollback scenarios restore the eligible previous data and commit identity, including sequence reuse after an intervening commit.
Zero/wrong/future/first IDs return CANT_ROLLBACK; no illegal consecutive rollback or intervening-operation sequence is used as a reference oracle.
Actual reopen sees restored data/IDs; callbacks and permitted quiet old-reader pointers/cursors remain valid.
Rollback retains native allocator high-water and counts reader setup without serializing ordinary readers; owned locks, snapshots and active aliases remain bounded.

24 corrupt descriptor/inventory/catalog/segment cases fail before selection without leaking pins or poisoning; correctly hash-sealed malformed user trees retain normal native-open lazy checks and fail full verify/export.
Quiet old-reader borrowed values and cursors remain valid through an eligible exclusive-use rollback and actual reopen; exact traced modern fixture includes these retained capabilities.

features.limits: Qualified for the exact Linux Legacy-backed C adapter artifact and pinned LMDB 1.0.2 exclusive-use contract. Combined 61-check/14-stage gate, native/C faults and allocator, namespace, integrity and reader-resource controls pass. Exact-file witnesses add one 256-byte metadata descriptor and zero data segments; A/B bytes, sizes and inodes remain unchanged. Ordinary-operation change budgets and controlled tail review pass. Rollback retains ordinary-open descriptor/inventory/file/catalog authentication with lazy checked user-tree access; full backup/check/export audits remain strict. Cost still scales with authenticated bytes: 731.859ms at 65,536 records in each of two databases versus reference0.029ms; no constant-time or operation-speed parity claim. WRITEMAP named-deletion reference assertions remain explicit exclusions. NOLOCK callers retain manual exclusion duties; Range/replica rollback remains unsupported. G03/G04/G05 and other backend qualification remain open. Evidence: conformance/features/m3-f02-f03-qualified.
